Portfolio Case Study

Catching a Missing Date of Service

Sometimes a claim can't be verified because a key detail is simply missing — not wrong, just not there. Approving a claim without confirming the date of service risks approving something outside the customer's actual coverage period.

Scenario: A customer called in to follow up on a reimbursement claim for a prescription, but the date of service field was missing from the submission — it didn't match anything on file to verify against. I followed up with the customer directly, and reached out to the provider as well to confirm the correct date, then cross-checked it against the customer's receipt to make sure both records matched before approving the claim.

How I caught and resolved it

🔎
Noticed the gap While reviewing the claim the customer called about, saw the date of service field was blank — a required detail I couldn't skip past.
📞
Followed up with the customer and provider Checked with the customer first, then contacted the pharmacy directly to confirm the correct date of service.
🧾
Matched it against the customer's receipt Compared the date the provider gave me with the customer's own receipt to confirm both records lined up.
✅
Updated and approved Once both sources matched, updated the claim record and approved it for reimbursement with confidence.
Outcome
Verified accuracy before approval — no assumptions made
Confirmed & Approved
